title: Concentration of activity in the hottest bytes: six published statistics restated as (share of bytes, share of activity)

units.y_activity_pct: % of activity (bandwidth, reuses or accesses, per row metric)

conventions: x = share of bytes, hottest first; y = share of the row's own activity metric carried by those bytes. Each row restates ONE published sentence; metrics, windows and populations differ, so rows must not be compared with each other. x_plot_pct is the marker position; lo/hi are the bar ends for range rows. Bounds: x '≤' means 'at most' (chevron points left); y '≥' means 'more than' (chevron points up).

mahar.cite: Mahar, Wang, Shu, Dhanotia, 'Workload Behavior Driven Memory Subsystem Design for Hyperscale', arXiv 2303.08396 (preprint)

wang.cite: Wang et al., 'KVCache Cache in the Wild', USENIX ATC'25, arXiv 2506.02634v5

hao.cite: Hao, Zhou, Yu, Stonebraker, 'Towards Buffer Management with Tiered Main Memory', SIGMOD'24 (PACMMOD 2(1), Art. 31)
hao.locator: PDF p.16 = p.31:16, Sec. 5.5 (Fig. 5b); setup Sec. 5.1 p.31:12

google.cite: Lagar-Cavilla et al., 'Software-Defined Far Memory in Warehouse-Scale Computers', ASPLOS'19
google.locator: PDF p.3 (Sec. 2, Fig. 1: 32% at T=120 s); PDF p.2 (Introduction: 1%-61% across clusters)

tpp.cite: Maruf et al., 'TPP: Transparent Page Placement for CXL-Enabled Tiered-Memory', ASPLOS'23, arXiv 2206.02878
tpp.locator: PDF p.3 (Introduction; characterised in Sec. 3.2, Fig. 7)

mooncake.cite: Qin et al., 'Mooncake: A KVCache-centric Disaggregated Architecture for LLM Serving', arXiv 2407.00079v4 (FAST'25)

rows.label: Meta services
rows.restatement: '90%-tile bandwidth is contributed by less than 10% of the memory capacity' read as: less than 10% of capacity (x <= 10) contributes ~90% of bandwidth (y ~ 90). Held for 30, 60 and 120 s windows per the paper; plotted window is 30 s.
rows.note: Quote: "Across the nine workloads, we observe that over 30 seconds, the active memory footprint is less than 25% of the total memory capacity, while the 90%-tile bandwidth is contributed by less than 10% of the memory capacity." Wording per notes/r2d M10: say '~90% of bandwidth from <10% of capacity', not 'P90 of bandwidth demand'. Paper's own bandwidth-percentile phrasing is retained as 'less than 10%'; the 10% is an upper bound, the 90% is a percentile level, not a measured point.

rows.label: Alibaba KV$
rows.population: KV$ blocks in a large cloud provider's LLM serving traces
rows.restatement: '10% of KV$ blocks contribute to 77% of the reuses' gives x = 10 (share of blocks, treated as share of bytes: blocks are fixed-size), y = 77.
rows.note: Quote: "The reuses follow a skewed distribution: 10 % of KV$ blocks contribute to 77 % of the reuses." Same paper notes the skew varies across traces. Block share equals byte share only if blocks are equal size (assumed; not verified in the paper text read).

rows.label: Hao et al.
rows.window: steady-state benchmark run (no fixed time window)
rows.population: YCSB-like benchmark, 23 GB workload, 10 threads, tiered buffer manager
rows.measured_or_emulated: emulated (remote memory emulated on CloudLab; zipfian skew 0.9)
rows.restatement: 'local memory size is only one sixth of remote memory' (3 GB local, 18 GB remote, Sec. 5.1) so local is 3/(3+18) = 1/7 = 14.3% of memory bytes; 'local memory serves more than half of the tuple accesses' gives y > 50 (dot at 50, upward chevron).
rows.loc: PDF p.16 = p.31:16, Sec. 5.5, Fig. 5b; sizes Sec. 5.1 p.31:12
rows.unc: derived: x = 3/(3+18) = 14.3%; alternatives 3/23 = 13.0% (share of the 23 GB workload) and 3/18 = 16.7% (local/remote); y is a lower bound only (exact rate is in Fig. 5b, not read)
rows.note: Quote: "even though local memory size is only one sixth of remote memory, local memory serves more than half of the tuple accesses (Figure 5b)." Setup quote: "The default workload size is 23 GB and the default local and remote memory sizes are 3 GB and 18 GB, respectively." Zipf 0.9 is the default benchmark skew (Sec. 5.1), so the skew is an input of the emulation, not a measured production property. The sentence refers to the large-memory setup; designs with a cache-replacement path (not 2T-MergedMem).

rows.label: Google fleet
rows.window: 120 s (cold = not accessed in T = 120 s)
rows.population: Google WSC fleet; range across clusters
rows.restatement: Cold = not accessed within 120 s, so all accesses in the window fall on the non-cold bytes. Fleet average 32% cold gives hot x = 100-32 = 68; across clusters 1%-61% cold gives hot x = 100-61 = 39 to 100-1 = 99; y = 100 by definition of cold.
rows.loc: PDF p.3 (Fig. 1 text) and PDF p.2 (Intro)
rows.unc: derived: x = 100 - cold%; range as published (cold 1-61% across clusters)
rows.note: Quotes: "At the most aggressive setting of T = 120 s, we observe that 32% of memory usage is cold" and "cold memory ranges from 1% to 61% across different clusters and from 1% to 52% even within the same cluster". Cold percent is a fraction of memory usage per job/machine averaged fleet-wide. y = 100 is definitional, not a measured bandwidth share.

rows.label: Meta TPP
rows.population: 4 production applications at Meta (Web, Cache, Data Warehouse families; TPP Sec. 3)
rows.restatement: '55-80% of an application's allocated memory remains idle within any two minutes interval': idle share 55-80% gives accessed share 100-80 = 20 to 100-55 = 45; all accesses in the window fall on the accessed pages, y = 100.
rows.unc: derived: x = 100 - idle%, idle 55-80% as published; y definitional
rows.note: Quote: "We characterize four popular applications in our production server fleet and find that 55-80% of an application's allocated memory remains idle within any two minutes interval (Sec. 3.2)." Marker position (32.5) is the midpoint of the bar and carries no extra information.

rows.label: Mooncake
rows.source: Qin et al., Mooncake, FAST'25 (arXiv v4)
rows.population: KV cache blocks in a sampled production-like trace
rows.measured_or_emulated: measured (trace from Kimi service; cache policy analysis is simulated)
rows.restatement: 'over 50% of cache blocks remaining unused' means the blocks that receive any hit are under 50% of blocks (x <= 50), and they receive all hits (y = 100). Blocks assumed equal size.
rows.loc: PDF p.8, Sec. 4.2, Fig. 6 (CDF of block hit count)
rows.unc: derived: x = 100 - (>50)% unused, so x < 50; y definitional
rows.note: Quote: "we observed a notable imbalance in cache block popularity, with over 50% of cache blocks remaining unused while certain blocks are accessed tens of thousands of times, as shown in Figure 6." The paper cautions the sample trace is a subset of real workloads. Fig. 6 not read for values; only the printed sentence is used.

reference.label: uniform access: no skew (e.g., dense weights, read every decode step)

extraction.method: Full texts rendered with pdftotext -layout; every quoted sentence located by grep and its PDF page confirmed by per-page search. Mahar, Wang, Mooncake and Lagar-Cavilla PDFs fetched to fulltext/ (arXiv versions v-latest as served 2026-10-03). No chart reads.

cross_check.max_disagreement: none on values; both note Hao denominator ambiguity (13-16.7%), Google per-cluster 1-61% vs per-machine 1-52%, and definitional y=100 for Google/TPP/Mooncake

caveats: Each point is a restatement of one published sentence; metrics (bandwidth, reuses, accesses), windows and populations differ, so points must not be compared with each other.
Rows 4-6 (Google, TPP, Mooncake) have y = 100 by definition of the cold/idle/unused statistic, not from a measured bandwidth share.
Mahar et al. is an arXiv preprint; the 10% is an upper bound ('less than') and 90% is the percentile level.
Hao et al. is emulated with a zipf 0.9 benchmark; x depends on denominator (13.0, 14.3 or 16.7%); 14.3% used.
Alibaba and Mooncake treat KV blocks as equal-size so block share equals byte share.
Mooncake sentence is from arXiv v4 (Sep 2025); wording not checked against the FAST'25 camera-ready.
